acceptance: A test shows a held plan posts a pending status and no decision
A test drives github.oracle_reviews through the paging call with more than one page
A test with more than 5 out-of-scope defects shows exactly 5 listed and the rest summarised
A test forces a long status description and asserts it is cut to 140 characters
The misnamed runner test is renamed or made to omit a status
Each new test fails when the rule it covers is disabled
context: Found in the completion audit of the oracle protocol on 2026-10-09. The marker size boundary is tracked separately in oracle-marker-patch-map-file-limit-20261009.
description:
A behaviour-by-behaviour audit of the oracle protocol tests on develop e7eb5ce7e found every named behaviour implemented and most covered, with these gaps:
1. A malformed or repeated marker makes the plan return `hold` (tested), but the finalize step that turns `hold` into a pending status (cli.py around line 449) is not: test_attempts.py::test_cli_finalize_fixed_decisions covers only `success` and `fork`.
2. test_cli_plan.py::test_more_than_a_hundred_reviews_are_all_read replaces github.oracle_reviews with a fake that returns 151 reviews, so nothing tests that the real call pages (`get_paginated`, `--paginate --slurp` in github.py).
3. The cap of 5 on defects listed as "not counted" (outside the changed files) is not tested; the only test uses one such defect.
4. No test forces a status description over 140 characters through report._clip.
5. test_runner.py::test_a_follow_up_missing_a_prior_status_is_recorded_for_the_judge passes a status through and never omits one; its name overstates it (the real coverage is test_rounds.py::test_a_prior_defect_with_no_status_stays_open).
6. The #2769 replay uses synthetic prior statuses and checks the planner and judge, not the posted review bodies.
